title: Assurance jury record v2 (DL-P0-171)
description: Human jury record for DESIGN-LAB's quality gate. It is a superset of the guarantees of design-lab/schemas/jury-record.schema.json (V1): jury_id -> jury_record_id, boundTreeSha (git short SHA) -> artifact_sha256 (exact nonzero artifact digest), humanReview{reviewer,date,verdict} -> juror{juror_id,kind,attestation} + decided_at (RFC3339 with offset), axes{5 named 1-5 integers} -> criteria[{criterion_id,weight,score,note}] with weights summing to 1, evidence[{level,artifact}] -> evidence_refs[], and verdict PASS/REVISE/REJECT -> ACCEPT/REVISE/REJECT. V1 additionally carried an inline 'deterministic' block that this v2 record omits on purpose: deterministic evidence is recorded as a DETERMINISTIC finding in assurance-qa-layer.schema.json and referenced here by evidence_refs, so a model or an agent cannot restate a rule result as part of a human verdict. The signing actor must be a HUMAN or PANEL juror; automation may only produce $defs/proposal, which cannot validate against this root because the roots differ in 'kind' and in their closed property sets.

subject_ref.description: The design subject the judgement is about (job, deliverable or artifact reference).

supersedes.description: Append-only edge to the jury_record_id this record replaces (never itself).

then.description: A rejection must cite at least one evidence_ref so it can be reviewed.
An unnamed panel is not a human actor.

sha256.description: Lowercase nonzero artifact digest; an all-zero digest is not a judged artifact.

rfc3339.description: RFC3339 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset. The module enforces this with a regex because the installed jsonschema has no date-time checker, and Python's fromisoformat would accept a bare date.

kind.description: Only a human or a named panel may sign; any agent/model/system kind is refused by the module.

attestation.description: How this human's judgement was obtained and witnessed; not a model summary of it.

members.description: Named humans in the panel; confidence stays null below two members.

score.description: 0-5, mirroring the V1 five-axis scale; 0 is only for a hard failure.

note.description: Required at either extreme score by allOf below; the module enforces the same rule.

proposal.title: JuryProposal (an agent suggestion; explicitly not a verdict)

is_verdict.description: Always false. A proposal is a recommendation and every function that accepts a verdict refuses it.
